gap: No result ChatGPT got states the arithmetic: uncompressed 4K at 144 Hz and 8-bit colour needs 31.35 Gb/s, which is 121% of the 25.92 Gb/s a DisplayPort 1.4 (HBR3) KVM can carry (151% at 10-bit). 4K at 120 Hz and 8-bit fills 99.6% of that link. So every DP 1.4 KVM's '4K144' claim depends on DSC, while an HDMI 2.1 48G link carries 4K144 at 10-bit uncompressed at 93% of its 42.0 Gb/s.
standout_why: I compared against the cited pages: TESmart's HDMI 2.1 gaming guide, TESmart's DSC blog, the Level1Techs KVM FAQ, and the Level1Techs single-monitor 2-computer store page. I also read the product pages ChatGPT showed (TESmart HKS201-M24). The L1 FAQ says 4K144 works 'because of DSC… Without DSC, no', and TESmart's DSC blog says 4K144 'often depends on timing and color settings'. So the conclusion is partly covered. None of these pages gives a Gb/s figure for 4K144, the 25.92 Gb/s HBR3 payload, or the HDMI 2.1 headroom. None explains why Level1Techs rates its switch at exactly 4K120 (99.6% of HBR3).
decides: On a DP 1.4 KVM (Level1Techs, TESmart DKS202-M24, StarTech D86A2, UGREEN 25962), 4K144 only works if DSC works end to end, Mac included. That is the very part ChatGPT kept telling the shopper to 'verify'. The finding favours connecting a MacBook Pro (M2 Pro/Max or later) from its own HDMI port, with no adapter, to an HDMI 2.1 48G KVM. That link has the headroom for 4K144 without compression. One catch: TESmart's HKS201-M24 page lists 4K144/165 as running 'through DSC' and makes no Mac claim, so no switch is proven to carry 4K144 uncompressed. This supports the current page's lead pick (use the monitor's built-in KVM, a direct link with no DSC middleman). It does not overturn it.
